A tactical battle at Bollaert-Delelis On May 10, 2026, Lens and Nantes clashed in a pivotal Ligue 1 fixture that demanded absolute concentration from both sides throughout the ninety minutes. Before a passionate crowd of 37,824, the match unfolded as a rigorous tactical test where defensive discipline ultimately outweighed offensive creativity. Establishing the rhythm The first half saw Lens dominate possession, with Andrija Bulatovic repeatedly whipping dangerous deliveries into the box from set-piece situations. Despite the sustained pressure, the Nantes defense held firm, with goalkeeper Robin Risser tasked with making a critical save to deny an Ignatius Ganago header. The tension was palpable as both managers adjusted their shapes, looking for a way to break the deadlock in a physical encounter. The VAR intervention The drama peaked in the second half when Lens thought they had found the breakthrough. Mezian Soares found the back of the net with a precise right-footed finish, seemingly handing his side the lead. However, the stadium fell silent as the referee turned to the VAR for a review. Following a deliberation, the goal was revoked due to an earlier foul, effectively neutralizing the most significant moment of the match. The closing minutes saw both teams exhaust their substitutions in a frantic search for a winner, but the final whistle confirmed a stalemate in a hard-fought league contest.

matches.title: Nice vs Lens
matches.description: Watch Nice vs Lens highlights and goals from Ligue 1 on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 3, 2026. The Ligue 1 season continued to deliver high-stakes drama on May 3, 2026 , as Nice hosted Lens in a match defined by tactical intrigue and moments of individual brilliance. With both sides desperate for points in the final stretch of the campaign, the atmosphere at the stadium was electric from the opening whistle, setting the stage for a physical and unpredictable encounter. A Cagey Opening at the Allianz Riviera The match began with both sides testing each other through set-pieces. Nice looked particularly dangerous early on, with Tom Louchet delivering several teasing corners that kept the Lens backline on high alert. In the 12th minute, a defensive blunder by Pierre Ganiou almost gifted the hosts an opener, but the visitors managed to scramble the ball clear. Juma Bah came closest for the home side in the 17th minute, rising highest to meet a Louchet cross, but his header was comfortably gathered by Robin Risser . Lens responded with pressure of their own, primarily through the delivery of Florian Thauvin , whose corners frequently caused chaos in the Nice penalty area. The game took a brief pause in the 21st minute as the referee consulted VAR for a potential penalty in favor of Nice , though play eventually resumed without a spot-kick being awarded. As the first half progressed, the contest turned increasingly physical; Malang Sarr was booked for unsportsmanlike conduct, and both Juma Bah and Florian Thauvin received yellow cards just before the interval as the intensity boiled over. Saint-Maximin Breaks the Deadlock The second half saw the deadlock finally broken in spectacular fashion. In the 60th minute, Adrien Thomasson found space in the middle of the park and threaded a pass to Allan Saint-Maximin . The mercurial forward, showing the flair that has made him a household name, unleashed a powerful left-footed strike from outside the box that beat the diving Yehvann Diouf to give Lens a 1-0 lead. The goal sparked a frantic response from Nice manager, who opted for a triple substitution in the 71st minute, introducing Ali Abdi , Isak Jansson , and Salis Abdul Samed to find a way back into the game. Lens looked to consolidate their lead, with Odsonne Edouard leading the line effectively before being replaced by Abdallah Sima . However, the momentum shifted dramatically in the 81st minute. Saud Abdulhamid , acting as the last man, committed a professional foul to stop a goal-scoring opportunity and was shown a straight red card. The dismissal left Lens vulnerable and forced them into a defensive shell for the closing stages. Late Drama and the Equalizer Capitalizing on their numerical advantage, Nice poured forward. The pressure told in the 84th minute when a loose ball in the box fell perfectly for the substitute Ali Abdi . The defender reacted quickest, stabbing the ball home with his left foot to send the home crowd into raptures and level the score at 1-1. The final minutes were played at a breakneck pace, with Adrien Thomasson receiving a yellow card for dissent as tensions flared between the players and the officials. In stoppage time, Nice pushed for a winner, with Kevin Carlos nearly connecting with a volley that flew just wide of the target. Melvin Bard was forced into a tactical foul to halt a late Lens counter-attack, earning himself a booking in the process. Despite the frantic end-to-end action and five minutes of added time, neither side could find a decisive third goal. The referee blew the whistle on a hard-fought draw that saw Lens finish with ten men and Nice walking away with a well-earned point thanks to their late resurgence.

matches.title: Lens vs Nice
matches.description: Watch Lens vs Nice highlights and goals from Coupe de France on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 22, 2026. On May 22, 2026, the Coupe de France atmosphere reached a fever pitch as Lens hosted Nice in front of a massive crowd of 76,000 spectators. The tension was palpable from the opening whistle, with both sides knowing that progression in the prestigious tournament was on the line. Lens Assert Dominance in an Explosive First Half The match ignited in the 25th minute when Lens broke the deadlock. Florian Thauvin , showcasing his clinical edge, found the back of the net with a well-placed left-footed strike following an assist from Matthieu Udol . The home side continued to press their advantage, and their persistence paid off again in the 42nd minute. This time, Thauvin turned provider, swinging in a corner that Odsonne Edouard expertly headed home to double the lead. However, Nice refused to go into the break quietly. Deep into first-half stoppage time, Jonathan Clauss delivered a dangerous corner from the left, which Djibril Coulibaly met with a powerful header to pull one back for the visitors. The late goal shifted the momentum, setting the stage for a compelling second period. Sima Provides the Decisive Blow The second half saw Nice controlling more of the ball as they searched for an equalizer, but the Lens defense, anchored by an outstanding performance from Pierre Ganiou , remained resolute. Tactical substitutions played a major role in the closing stages, and it was the introduction of Abdallah Sima that proved inspired. In the 78th minute, Sima found space in the box and fired home with his right foot to restore a two-goal cushion for the hosts. As the clock ticked down, the match grew increasingly physical. The referee was kept busy, issuing yellow cards to Kojo Peprah Oppong , Morgan Sanson , and Matthieu Udol in a frantic final sequence. Despite late pressure from Nice , Lens held firm to secure the victory. Florian Thauvin left the pitch as a primary contender for Man of the Match, having been central to nearly every positive move for his side.

matches.title: Lyon vs Lens
matches.description: Watch Lyon vs Lens highlights and goals from Ligue 1 on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 17, 2026. The stadium lights shone brightly as Lyon hosted Lens for a highly anticipated Ligue 1 clash on May 17, 2026. Both sides took to the pitch knowing that every tactical decision and individual moment of brilliance would define their trajectory in the league standings. A Blistering Start for Lens The match ignited with high physical intensity, marked as early as the 5th minute by a yellow card for Malang Sarr . It did not take long for Lens to translate their early pressure into a tangible advantage. In the 20th minute, Wesley Said opened the scoring with a clinical right-footed finish, following a decisive pass from Kyllian Antonio . This breakthrough bolstered the visitors' confidence, allowing them to exploit gaps in the Lyon defense while the hosts struggled to respond despite several corners delivered by Endrick and Afonso ira . The visitors' dominance intensified as the half-hour mark approached. Wesley Said remained the central figure, doubling his tally in the 32nd minute with a sharp left-footed strike assisted by Amadou Haidara . Lyon appeared dazed by the opposition's efficiency, and their situation grew more dire in first-half stoppage time. Florian Sotoca capitalized on a setup from Florian Thauvin to net a third goal, leaving the home side with a massive mountain to climb in the second period. Tactical Adjustments and Thauvin’s Brilliance The start of the second half saw a flurry of tactical changes, with Lyon introducing Hans Hateboer and Roman Yaremchuk , while Lens brought on Ruben Aguilar and Matthieu Udol . However, the momentum remained firmly with the visitors. In the 54th minute, Florian Thauvin produced the highlight of the night with a magnificent left-footed lob that extended the lead to 4-0, courtesy of an Andrija Bulatovic assist. This goal effectively settled the contest, allowing Lens to control the tempo for the remainder of the match. Despite desperate attempts from Lyon to find a consolation goal, with Afonso ira and substitute Ernest Nuamah trying to create danger from set-pieces, the Lens backline remained disciplined. The closing stages saw the game turn more physical, resulting in bookings for Pavel Sulc , Ruben Aguilar , and Nidal Celik . At the final whistle, Lens celebrated a categorical and deserved victory, showcasing a level of clinical finishing that left Lyon with no answers in front of their home crowd.

matches.title: Lens vs Paris SG
matches.description: Watch Lens vs Paris Saint Germain highlights and goals from Ligue 1 on ReFooty: Football Highlights Hub. Match played on May 13, 2026. On the evening of May 13, 2026 , the lights of the stadium illuminated a high-stakes Ligue 1 battle between Lens and Paris Saint-Germain . Fans gathered in anticipation of a tactical chess match that would test the resolve and clinical nature of both squads until the final whistle. Clinical Efficiency in the First Half The match ignited with a frantic intensity as Lens looked to impose their rhythm on home soil. The first major opening arrived in the 20th minute when Adrien Thomasson managed to get a shot away, only to see his effort heroically hacked off the goal line. This wake-up call spurred Paris Saint-Germain into action, as they began to dominate possession and probe for weaknesses. The breakthrough came in the 29th minute following a defensive lapse by Malang Sarr . Ousmane Dembele pounced on the error to provide the assist for Khvicha Kvaratskhelia , who coolly finished with his right foot to give the visitors the lead. Lens Pressure and VAR Drama Lens emerged for the second half determined to find a way back into the contest. Matthieu Udol threatened with a powerful header that was comfortably gathered by Matvey Safonov , while a flurry of substitutions from the hosts added fresh energy to their forward line. In the 75th minute, the equalizer seemed certain, but Abdallah Sima saw his strike rebound off the post. The tension reached a boiling point in the 88th minute when the referee paused play for a VAR check on a potential Lens goal. However, Florian Thauvin was ruled offside, leaving the home supporters in despair. Late Counter-Attack Seals the Points As Lens committed bodies forward in a desperate search for a late leveler, Paris Saint-Germain exploited the space left behind with a lethal counter-attack. In the third minute of stoppage time, Desire Doue broke forward and teed up young Ibrahim Mbaye , who finished clinically to double the lead. Despite a late scare involving a Lucas Beraldo blunder and a Thauvin effort that whistled inches wide of the post, the champions-elect held firm to secure a 2-0 victory, showcasing their ability to punish opponents in decisive moments.
